title: Lifting a quotient basis over an infinitesimal Hopf subalgebra
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. A commutative Hopf $k$-algebra here means a unital commutative $k$-algebra $A$ with $k$-algebra maps $\Delta_A:A\to A\otimes_k A$, $\epsilon_A:A\to k$, $S_A:A\to A$ such that $(\Delta_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\Delta_A)\Delta_A$, $(\epsilon_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=(1\otimes\epsilon_A)\Delta_A=1_A$, and $\mu_A(S_A\otimes1)\Delta_A=\mu_A(1\otimes S_A)\Delta_A=\eta_A\epsilon_A$, under the usual tensor unit and associativity identifications; $\mu_A$ and $\eta_A$ are multiplication and unit. Tensor products are those of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. A Hopf homomorphism $u:P\to Q$ means a $k$-algebra homomorphism with $\Delta_Qu=(u\otimes u)\Delta_P$, $\epsilon_Qu=\epsilon_P$ and $S_Qu=uS_P$. Let $A,B$ be commutative Hopf $k$-algebras, both finitely generated as $k$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $i:A\to B$ be an injective Hopf homomorphism. Write $I=\ker\epsilon_A$, and assume $I^n=0$ for an integer $n\geq1$. Give $B$ the $A$-module structure through $i$. For any set $J$ and family $(e_j)_{j\in J}$ in $B$ whose residue classes form a $k$-vector-space basis of $B/(i(I)B)$, the $A$-linear map
$$\bigoplus_{j\in J}A\longrightarrow B,\qquad(a_j)\longmapsto\sum_j i(a_j)e_j$$
is an isomorphism. Here a basis and the direct-sum module mean the unique finite-linear-combination convention of [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and $i(I)B$ denotes the ideal generated by $i(I)$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. The index set $J$ need not be finite.

source.place: Theorem 3.31, printed pp.73--74, nilpotent-augmentation case: the explicitly asserted isomorphism A^(J) to B. The printed proof of injectivity has a gap: see report.md, Source error; this new node records the true statement only, not that argument.

proof.text: Choose algebra generators $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ of $A$ using [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Put $y_l=x_l-\epsilon_A(x_l)1$. These still generate $A$, and every $y_l$ lies in $I$. Every monomial in the $y_l$ of total degree at least $n$ lies in $I^n=0$. Thus the finitely many monomials of total degree less than $n$ span $A$ over $k$. Extracting a basis from this finite spanning family shows that $A$ admits a finite $k$-basis. This includes $m=0$ and $n=1$, when $A=k$.

source.place: Theorem 3.31, p.73, nilpotent-augmentation case; elementary finite-dimensionality observation for the repair.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-hopf-self-injective] with $H=A$, $U=A$, $V=B$, $j=i$ and $f=1_A$. Step 1 gives its finite-dimensional hypothesis; $i$ is injective and is $A$-linear for the specified action on $B$. The result is an $A$-linear retraction $r:B\to A$ satisfying $ri=1_A$.

source.place: Theorem 3.31, pp.73--74, repair of the invalid summand argument; Bichon section 3 supplies the separately stated self-injectivity input.

proof.text: The Hopf compatibility $\Delta_B i=(i\otimes i)\Delta_A$ implies the coideal condition: if $\Delta_A(a)=\sum a_l\otimes a_l^{\prime}$, then $\Delta_B(i(a))=\sum i(a_l)\otimes i(a_l^{\prime})$ is the image of $\sum a_l\otimes i(a_l^{\prime})\in A\otimes_k B$. Together with the retraction of step 2, [lem-sfb-split-coideal-faithfully-flat] shows that $B$ is faithfully flat over $A$, hence flat by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Commutativity is essential here: $r(i(a)b i(a^{\prime}))=a r(b)a^{\prime}$ is the bimodule retraction required by the source.

source.place: Theorem 3.31, pp.73--74, replacement justification for injectivity of c; Bichon Theorem 1.1 specialized to commutative algebras.

proof.text: Let $F=\bigoplus_J A$ with coordinate vectors $v_j$, and let $q:F\to B$ send $v_j$ to $e_j$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. If $L=q(F)$, the residue-basis hypothesis gives $B=L+IB$. Consequently $C=B/L$ satisfies $C=IC$, so repeated substitution gives $C=I^n C=0$. Thus $q$ is surjective. The same residue-basis hypothesis says that the induced map $F/IF\to B/IB$ is injective as well as surjective: an element of $F/IF$ is a finite family of scalars in $A/I=k$. Put $N=\ker q$. This injectivity implies $N\subseteq IF$.

source.place: Theorem 3.31, p.73, nilpotent generation and the map on residue quotients, with no finiteness assumption on J.

proof.text: Tensor the exact sequence $N\to F\xrightarrow{q}B\to0$ with $I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], the kernel of $1_I\otimes q:I\otimes_A F\to I\otimes_A B$ is the image of $I\otimes_A N$. Write $\mu_M:I\otimes_A M\to M$ for multiplication, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Flatness of $B$ and [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], applied to $I\hookrightarrow A$, make $\mu_B$ injective under $A\otimes_A B\simeq B$. For $x\in N\subseteq IF$, choose $u\in I\otimes_A F$ with $\mu_F(u)=x$. Then $\mu_B((1_I\otimes q)(u))=q(x)=0$, so $(1_I\otimes q)(u)=0$. Right exactness gives $w\in I\otimes_A N$ mapping to $u$. Multiplication sends $w$ to an element of $IN$ whose image in $F$ is $x$. Hence $N\subseteq IN$, while $IN\subseteq N$ holds because $N$ is a submodule. Thus $N=IN$.

source.place: Theorem 3.31, pp.73--74, tensor diagram chased explicitly after repairing injectivity of c. Right exactness is Stacks algebra.tex, Tag 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact.

proof.text: Iterating $N=IN$ gives $N=I^nN=0$. Therefore $q$ is injective as well as surjective, so it is an $A$-module isomorphism. This is exactly the asserted map on finite-support families. Neither the generation argument nor the kernel argument required $J$ finite.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NC-7ea33122f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, the parent lem-sfb-hopf-subalgebra-faithfully-flat, every cited statement, and Milne Theorem 3.31 (printed pp.73-74). The source error is confirmed. Milne's claim that I_A is a direct summand of A holds only over k, so injectivity of c is unjustified. Counterexample: for A=k[t]/(t^2) in characteristic 2, any A-linear p:A->(t) has p(t)=t p(1)=0. The statement is kept verbatim. Steps 1-6 check out. Step 1: monomials in y_l=x_l-eps(x_l) of degree below n span A, so A is finite-dimensional. Step 2: the self-injective node with U=A, V=B, j=i, f=1 gives an A-linear retraction r. Step 3: Delta_B i=(i⊗1)(sum a_l⊗i(a'_l)) is the coideal condition, and commutativity makes r a bimodule map; this matches the Bichon arXiv:2301.05480v2 abstract (right coideal subalgebra that is an A-bimodule direct summand gives faithful flatness). def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map then gives flatness. Step 4: B=L+IB, C=I^nC=0, and F/IF to B/IB is bijective, so N is in IF. Step 5: right exactness (lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact), injectivity of mu_B by flatness, and naturality give N=IN. Step 6: N=I^nN=0. J may be infinite throughout. The new nodes are statement-only, self-contained and true. Self-injectivity of finite-dimensional Hopf algebras is the Larson-Sweedler Frobenius property. For the coideal criterion I tested A=B, A=k, and k[x] in k[x^{±1}], which is correctly excluded because no retraction exists. Neither node restates the item or the parent. A whole-DAG search found no duplicate (self-injective, Frobenius, coideal, conditional expectation, 126 Hopf nodes).
